stimuli.text:
A `Thermostat` keeps a temperature setting between a minimum and a maximum, inclusive.


• `Thermostat(int min, int max, int start)` creates a thermostat. Precondition: min <= start <= max.

• `void raise(int amount)` and `void lower(int amount)` change the setting by amount, but never past max or min.

• `int getSetting()` returns the current setting.

• `int getChanges()` returns how many calls to raise or lower actually changed the setting.

Example:

```java
Thermostat t = new Thermostat(11, 22, 13);
t.raise(10);      // setting is 22
t.raise(1);      // still 22: no change
t.lower(4);      // setting is 18
t.getSetting();  // returns 18
t.getChanges();  // returns 2
```

questions.stem:
Consider the following code segment.

```java
int x = (int) (Math.random() * 15) + -1;
```

Which of the following describes all possible values of x?

options.why: Math.random() never returns 1, so the product is always less than 15.
Correct. Math.random() * 15 is in [0, 15); truncating gives 0 to 14, then -1 is added.
The truncated value can be 0.
The largest truncated value is 14.

questions.explanation: `(int) (Math.random() * 15)` is an integer from 0 to 14; adding -1 gives -1 to 13.
